title: Non-soficity of OpenAI's torsion-free hyperbolic group
description: Is every word-hyperbolic group sofic? OpenAI recently constructed a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group G that is not residually finite, with a Lean formalization. We show that G is not sofic. Their rank argument against finite quotients uses a quotient only through its permutation matrices, and it survives approximation: a relation that fails on a small fraction of points costs a small rank error, and a word with few fixed points costs a small trace error. So approximate permutation models are excluded at a fixed positive accuracy, while soficity would supply them at every accuracy; moreover, one fixed nonidentity element of G dies in every sofic quotient. We formalize the conclusion in Lean on top of OpenAI's development: some torsion-free word-hyperbolic group is not sofic. The same rectangles and the same finite-field certificate exclude Linnell division rings: for every division ring K of the characteristic q fixed by the construction, neither K[G] nor the group ring over K of any group containing G has a Linnell division ring. Freeness of certain line subgroups would force full rank, while the certificate forces the rank to collapse; no zero divisor is exhibited. OpenAI's torsion-free groups with zero divisors, or with a group algebra that is not directly finite, already show that Linnell division rings need not exist in characteristic two; here the group is G itself. We also split G as a free product of a free group and a torsion-free hyperbolic group that again has no Linnell division ring in characteristic q, and we show where the argument stops short of hyperlinearity, including a barrier for unitary models with bounded denominators. The group and every input to the non-soficity argument are OpenAI's.
